articles.title: Malviya Nagar hotel fire: Delhi HC seeks report on hotel owner's health
articles.summary:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday sought a report from the Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital here regarding the health of the jailed owner of a Malviya Nagar hotel where a fire claimed 23 lives in June.
Justice Manoj Jain passed the order on a plea by Lovkesh Bajaj seeking interim bail in the case on the grounds that he was suffering from intestinal obstructions and his condition was "serious".
Noting that Bajaj was admitted in the hospital since August 24, Justice Jain directed, "Let a comprehensive report be sought form the RML Hospital."
The court listed the matter for hearing tomorrow.
Bajaj, presently in judicial custody, is named as an accused in the case over the fire at the five-storey 'Flourish Stay' B&B in Hauz Rani on June 3, in which 23 people were killed, while 24 others suffered grievous injuries.
On September 3, a trial court rejected his plea seeking interim bail of four weeks on medical grounds, saying he was already receiving adequate specialised medical treatment .

articles.title: 3 countries threaten to break away from UK
articles.summary: The leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland signed a pact Monday that threatens to lead to the breakup of the United Kingdom.The first ministers of the three semiautonomous regions of the UK told Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his government to prepare for constitutional change and that their future lies with the European Union."For people watching across these islands - for people watching around the world - there could be no clearer sign that Westminster's time is coming to an end," they said in a memorandum of understanding, referring to Parliament.The announcement came about 48 hours after US President Donald Trump waded into the waters of the politically contentious issue when he said he would "love to see" a reunified Ireland during a trip to visit his golf course hosting the Irish Open.It's the first time the leaders of all three countries are either from pro-independence parties, or pro-unification in the case of Northern Ireland, which was partitioned and remained part of the UK when Ireland won independence from Britain over a century ago.Burnham's spokesperson brushed aside the threat and said the prime minister strongly believes in the union and was more focused on lowering the cost of living than dealing with constitutional debates."The United Kingdom is at its best when people come together around our shared values and problem-solving, rather than division," Tom Wells said.Nicola McEwen, director of the University of Glasgow Centre for Public Policy, said the summit was symbolically important but has no legal significance."I don't see the threat to the union being bigger today than it was yesterday," McEwen said.In the late 1990s, the UK passed legislative acts that decentralised government through the process of devolution, giving each country except England some level of policy independence and self-governance through their own parliaments.But tensions have remained with the UK-wide government in London, which retained control over national issues and those concerning England.Scotland's John Swinney and Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill called for independence referendums in their countries, while Rhun ap Iorwerth did not provide a timetable for one in Wales.The three leaders appeared in their political capacity, rather than their official one, possibly because O'Neill is in a power-sharing government with the Democratic Unionist Party.Northern Ireland's Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly, of the DUP, accused O'Neill, of the Sinn Fein party, of "weaponising" the role of first minister by signing the agreement."I am first minister in the north of Ireland," O'Neill replied. "This is about historic change happening all around us."Scotland tried unsuccessfully to break away in 2014, with voters rejecting a referendum 55 per cent to 45 per cent. But McEwen said support for Scottish independence has grown since Brexit, in which the UK formally left the European Union in January 2020, following a referendum in June 2016.Swinney, leader of the Scottish National Party, said he believed voters would now vote for independence if the UK government approved a referendum.Burnham told Parliament last week he would allow such a vote to be held if there was a "clear consensus" in Scotland, but later sent Swinney a letter saying a vote was "off limits".The 1998 Good Friday peace accord that ended three decades of sectarian violence in Northern Ireland known as "The Troubles," requires a vote on unification if polls there indicate it would likely pass, a threshold the UK government says has not been met. Ireland would also have to approve the change in a referendum.Burnham has made devolution a major theme since taking office less than two months ago, but his focus has been on regional governments across England, a reflection of his years as mayor of Greater Manchester.Swinney tried to turn Burnham's ideology to his advantage, saying his frequent talk of devolution "leads you to the logic of recognising the right of the people of Scotland, in my case, to decide their own future".Beyond any threat of departing the union, McEwen said the greatest impact of the three joining forces could be that they agreed to cooperate with each other routinely and that could help to exert more influence on the UK government."It does keep on the agenda that question about, well, if the United Kingdom is a union based on consent, what is the pathway where it looks like that consent may no longer be there?" McEwen said. "Any UK government has been very reluctant to engage in that discussion."

articles.title: Govt may use your data to draw financial info
articles.summary: New Delhi: The government plans to leverage the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India's (Cersai) expanding database to further strengthen credit oversight and risk monitoring in the financial sector.The move coincides with the phased rollout of the Central KYC Records Registry, or CKYCRR 2.0, said people familiar with the developments. "There is a view that Cersai (central online database)can expand its role from only being limited to a registry-maintaining body to a more advanced data-driven analytical institution," said an executive aware of the developments. The repository body can consider developing its internal strength and issue analytical reports and products on the lines of the Insurance Information Bureau of India, or IIB, he said. The insurance industry currently utilises IIB products such as Sudharshan and Kavach for underwriting, claims processing and fraud detection.134247311"These are very early discussions, but the idea is to use this data across various segments including customer insights so that financial institutions can offer more targeted products besides fraud prevention," the executive said. Last week, the Reserve Bank of India issued draft guidelines on standard operating procedure (SOP) to be deployed by banks for placing temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts linked to money-mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds.The government had in the FY26 budget announced plans to simplify KYC norms and start a streamlined mechanism for periodic updating, particularly for low-risk customers. "Some of these improved models have already been rolled out, and now, as we have more real-time updates, such datasets can also be used to generate insights on interconnected exposures and potential fraud risks," said another executive, requesting anonymity.Earlier this month, in a letter to all reporting entities, the Central KYC Records Registry said CKYCRR 2.0 will go live soon and that they should ensure sufficient transactions are undertaken during the pilot testing window to establish the robustness of the end-to-end process. Oasis announce 38-date 'Live '27' tour
articles.summary: Oasis, the defining rock band of the 1990s Britpop era, announced a 38-date tour for 2027 spanning Britain, Ireland, mainland Europe and the United States on Monday, Reuters reported.Billed as "Live '27," the run marks the band's first major tour since their blockbuster 2025 reunion, and comes with a reworked ticketing process designed to avoid a repeat of the chaos that marred that comeback.A new ticketing system after 2025's fiascoTo avoid a repeat of the ticketing fiasco that accompanied the Gallagher brothers' first comeback in 2025, fans will have to register for a chance to buy tickets rather than compete in an open general sale, Reuters reported.Registration closes on Thursday, September 17, and successful applicants will be sent a unique, non-transferable code granting access to a specific on-sale window, with the UK sale spread across three separate windows a day on September 25, 26 and 27.Even members of Oasis's own mailing list must register, and there will be no general public sale outside this process. Standard ticket prices will be fixed and range between £71.50 ($96.50) and £266.60, including fees, promoters said.The new approach follows sharp criticism of the general sale for the band's 2025 reunion tour, when dynamic pricing caused ticket costs to jump while fans queued, and roughly 14 million people submitted requests for just 1.4 million tickets across the 17 shows on sale at the time, according to concert industry data.Oasis said at the time that ticketing and pricing decisions were left entirely to their promoters and management, and that they had not known dynamic pricing would be used.In a statement, Oasis said, "Start the celebrations," adding they would "once again return to lift the spirits of the people." "Come witness the fitness," the statement continued. "It shall be a sight to behold."Where and when they will playThe band will start Live '27 with five shows in Glasgow in May, before moving to Manchester, their home city in northern England, for 11 dates at the Etihad Stadium, Reuters reported. Dates in Munich, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Paris, Rome, Boston and Las Vegas follow, along with a stop at Slane Castle in Ireland, before Oasis close the tour with four shows in Knebworth, southern England, in September, the site of two legendary 1996 concerts where the band played to a combined 250,000 fans.Oasis were the biggest guitar band of the 1990s, according to Reuters. Their 1994 debut album, "Definitely Maybe," was an instant hit, and its follow-up, "(What's the Story) Morning Glory?", went on to become the decade's biggest-selling record, powered by hits including "Wonderwall" and "Don't Look Back in Anger." Tension between Noel Gallagher, the band's main songwriter, and his younger brother, lead singer Liam, led to the band's split in 2009.From breakup to blockbuster reunionNews in 2024 that the brothers were reuniting sparked a frenzy for tickets, with thousands of fans enduring hours in online queues only to find prices had risen by the time they reached the front of the line, Reuters reported.Despite the rocky start, the band's return to the stage in Cardiff in 2025 delighted both fans and critics, who said the group sounded as strong as it ever had.The reunion tour ultimately grew into a 41-date run across 14 countries, drawing a combined attendance of roughly 2.89 million fans and generating an estimated $525.3 million at the box office, with support from acts including Cage the Elephant and Richard Ashcroft.A documentary chronicling the reunion, titled "Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger," premiered at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month.(With inputs from Reuters)

articles.title: India, China agree to address trade concerns
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met Chinese counterpart Wang Wentao on Monday wherein they agreed to implement the important consensus reached by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting on the sidelines of BRICS Summit.The two leaders, in a bilateral meeting held on Saturday, had agreed to "expand mutually beneficial cooperation in the economic and trade fields, properly address each other's economic and trade concerns in a balanced manner, and better benefit enterprises and people of both countries," Spokesperson of Chinese Embassy in India Yu Jing said in post on X.Also read: Xi-Modi thaw warms up ties at BRICS, but old India-China fault lines remainThe two leaders had a sincere and in-depth exchange of views and reached the important consensus that China and India should be partners.According to an earlier statement released by Chinese Embassy Spokesperson Xu Feihong, Xi had pointed out that China always approaches and develops its relations with India from a strategic and long-term perspective.The Chinese president said India and China should view each other as partners rather than rivals, and development opportunities rather than threats, as the two countries seek to place bilateral ties on a steadier footing. He called for an “objective and rational strategic perception” of the relationship, saying both sides should draw on each other’s strengths, support each other and pursue common development.Xi noted that institutional exchanges between the two countries had gradually resumed over the past two years, while the areas of cooperation had expanded and bilateral trade had reached a new high. He described the progress as having “not come easily” and urged both sides to cherish the current situation.On economic ties, Xi called for development to remain the “greatest common denominator” between the two countries, with greater emphasis on friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation. He also called for expanding people-to-people exchanges and direct flights to improve public perceptions of bilateral relations, while addressing each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced manner.Also read: Xi Jinping’s five-point BRICS plan puts China’s tech ambitions in spotlightThe Chinese president also linked the future of bilateral ties to progress on the boundary question, calling for “mutual respect and mutual understanding” to resolve irritants. Both sides should pursue parallel and mutually reinforcing progress on the relationship and boundary talks while maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas, he said.On the broader global role of India and China, Xi called for greater coordination in multilateral forums, including BRICS, the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the G20. He urged the two countries to support each other’s BRICS chairships, work together to address global challenges and uphold what he described as international fairness and justice.He also framed closer India-China cooperation in the context of the Global South, saying the two most populous countries and important members of the Global South have a responsibility to contribute to world peace, stability, development and prosperity.During their conversation on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit 2026, PM Modi conveyed to Xi Jinping that peace and tranquillity along the border remains essential for development of India-China relations, emphasising that existing agreements on border management must be strictly observed.The prime minister highlighted that both sides must be "guided by three aspects -- mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest" in the ties.

articles.summary: New Delhi: The average all-India retail price of sugar remained below Rs 60 per kg for the fourth straight day on Monday following a series of government measures, even as festive demand put upward pressure on prices in some regions.On Monday, the average retail sugar price stood at Rs 59.57 per kg, marginally up from Rs 58.99 per kg on the previous day. Sugar prices dropped below the Rs 60 per kg level on Friday and eased further in the last three days, according to data maintained by the Consumer Affairs Ministry.Also read: India's retail inflation quickens to 4.8% in August from 4.45% in July as food prices exert pressureHowever, the average retail price remains higher than Rs 58.23 per kg, recorded on August 21, when the Centre first allowed sugar imports and took other steps to rein in sweetener prices.The maximum retail price, however, remained firm at Rs 85 per kg, while the minimum was Rs 40 per kg on Monday, the ministry data showed.Among the southern states, retail prices edged up in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, while Tamil Nadu and Kerala saw a marginal decline.In Andhra Pradesh, the average retail price rose to Rs 55.56 per kg on Monday from Rs 49.58 per kg on August 21, while in Kerala it inched up to Rs 57.8 per kg from Rs 56.75 per kg over the same period.In the major sugar-producing states, prices eased. articles.title: US-Iran war sends rice prices higher in India
articles.summary: Rice, a staple on Indian plates, is getting pricier as the US-Iran war drives countries to lock in food supplies, pushing up global demand. Basmati prices have risen 15–20% in the first quarter of FY27 from a year earlier, while non-basmati varieties are up 20–25%, squeezed by stronger overseas demand and deficient rains in southern India.Prices are likely to stay high until the new crop arrives in October-November, leaving consumers with little chance of near-term relief.“Globally, all the countries are trying to secure their food supply. Rice being one of the major staples, they are buying aggressively. The Gulf countries are buying huge quantities of rice from India,” said Suraj Agarwal, CEO of RiceVilla group, a rice exporting and marketing firm saidThe surge in demand has pushed basmati rice, widely used in biryani, to around Rs 100 per kg in the first quarter of FY27, from Rs 85 per kg in the same period last year. The increase has also extended to non-basmati varieties, putting pressure on household budgets.Sona Masoori rice, which was priced at Rs 51-52 per kg last year, has risen to Rs 63-64 per kg. Agarwal said prices are unlikely to ease in the near term as the market is stretched between strong demand and limited fresh supplies.“Prices are unlikely to come down any time soon. The US-Iran truce treaty is yet to happen, and the arrival of the kharif crop is almost two to three months away,” Agarwal said.The export market continues to provide strong support to basmati prices. Akshay Gupta, head of bulk rice exports, KRBL Limited, said the demand for Indian basmati remains strong, with India shipping a record 6.52 million tonnes in FY26 to 154 countries.Saudi Arabia remains the largest buyer, while enquiries from West Asia continue to be high. However, payment and shipping disruptions along the Gulf corridor have slowed shipments, creating a backlog of demand rather than weakening buying interest.“The 2025 crop moved faster than anyone expected and there is very little carry-out going into the October arrivals. Domestic prices are being set by that tightness, not by exports,” Gupta said.The domestic market is also facing pressure from government procurement and uneven rainfall. BV Krishna Rao, president of the Rice Exporters Association, said government buying for public distribution has contributed to the price rise.“In Telangana, the government is distributing non-basmati rice through PDS. Also, lesser rains in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana have kept the prices firm,” Rao said.With the next kharif crop still weeks away, traders expect prices to remain elevated through the immediate term. Any meaningful correction is likely to depend on fresh crop arrivals, improvement in rainfall and a moderation in overseas buying. Until then, consumers are likely to bear the brunt of higher rice prices.
